blocks.text: Coquitlam Mobile Homes for Sale: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Coquitlam has a dedicated mobile-home park zone. Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 lists RMH-1, Mobile Home Park, among the City's zones, and a home's siting must comply with that bylaw and the Building Bylaw.

Moving or placing a home needs City permits and provincial documents. The City's Mobile Home Guide requires a building permit to move a home into or within a Coquitlam park, a current Manufactured Home Registry document, proof of Canadian Standards Association (CSA) Z240 compliance, the park manager's written approval, and a provincial transit permit under the Mobile Home Act.
Recreational trailers are not homes here: the City guide states recreational-type trailers are not permitted to be used as a residence.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Mobile Homes for Sale: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: A sale is only effective once registered in the Manufactured Home Registry, filed through a lawyer or notary with the signed bill of sale — a missing CSA certification label on the home is a financing and resale flag.
Even Hideaway Park's postal code varies across listing sources for 4200 Dewdney Trunk Road, so verify the civic address against City or registry records, never a listing.
Coquitlam utility penalties run on a different calendar from taxes: 5 percent after March 31 and again after October 1 for utilities, versus July 2 and September 15 for taxes.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Mobile Homes for Sale: costs and taxes

items.t: The City approved a 2026 property tax increase of $93 a year for the average household, 3.37 percent, with utilities included taking the total to $137 a year.

The Speculation and Vacancy Tax (SVT) applies in Coquitlam, because the Province lists the City of Coquitlam as a designated taxable area — confirm with the Province and the Registry how it treats a chattel home on a rented pad for a specific purchase.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Mobile Homes for Sale: getting around

items.t: Maillardville's two parks sit on Cayer Street and King Edward Street, in the southwest city near the Lougheed corridor, while Hideaway Park sits on Dewdney Trunk Road in Central Coquitlam — two separate transit grounds, so check the route for the specific park address.

blocks.text: Coquitlam Mobile Homes for Sale: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check park conversion risk first, because it is the tenure risk unique to this home type.
Verify the home's Registry record and CSA label before financing, because the City will not permit a home without CSA Z240 compliance evidence and the sale is not effective until registered.

faq.a: A home on a rented pad is not land ownership — the buyer owns the manufactured home as a chattel and rents the pad from the park owner, under a Manufactured Home Park Tenancy Act tenancy, so the purchase, financing and resale all run through the Manufactured Home Registry, not a land title.
faq.q: What do I actually own when I buy in a Coquitlam park?

faq.a: By the provincial cap plus a proportional amount, once a year. For an increase taking effect in 2026 the cap is 2.3 percent plus the proportional amount for changes in local government levies and regulated utility fees, and for 2027 it is 2.2 percent plus the proportional amount — percentages only, with no pad-rent dollar figure stated here.
faq.q: How much can my pad rent go up?

faq.a: Only with permits and approvals in place first.
